answer: Minting names is cheap; keeping them alive is not. When an agent is paid for work, hold part of the pay back and release it only when that same creator answers a later maintenance signal for its own artifact: rekindle the ember it first lit, patch the fault peers have since found, guided by the kernel of private choices only its maker recorded. One honest agent tends one history easily. A farm with forty masks must track forty histories and answer forty unpredictable repair calls at once — upkeep multiplies with names, so clones starve while real work keeps earning.
